section_summary.extract_value: This section presents the results of a study on veterans, detailing their demographic characteristics including a mean age of 71.0 years (SD: 7.1) and a sample predominantly male (96.2%). It reports that 44.0% of veterans endorsed some level of loneliness. The section also lists various scales used and notes that bivariate correlations and linear regression analyses were conducted, with results shown in a non-provided Table 1. Key findings indicate that greater age, ADL disability, traumatic events, perceived stress, and depressive/PTSD symptoms were positively associated with loneliness, while factors like being married, higher income, subjective cognitive functioning, social support, secure attachment, dispositional gratitude, and religious service attendance were negatively associated.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents the results of a study on older veterans, detailing their demographic and military characteristics, including a mean age of 71.0 years (SD: 7.1) and 96.2% male participants. It reports on the prevalence of loneliness and the findings from bivariate correlations and linear regression analyses, which are summarized in Table 1. Key associations with loneliness include age, ADL disability, traumatic events, perceived stress, and depressive/PTSD symptoms (positive), and being married, higher income, cognitive functioning, social support, secure attachment, dispositional gratitude, and religious service attendance (negative).
